Legal information
Warning notice system
This manual contains notices you have to observe in order to ensure your personal safety, as well as to prevent damage 
to property. The notices referring to your personal safety are highlighted in the manual by a safety alert symbol, notices 
referring only to property damage have no safety alert symbol. These notices shown below are graded according to 
the degree of danger.
DANGER
indicates that death or severe personal injury will result if proper precautions are not taken.
WARNING
indicates that death or severe personal injury may result if proper precautions are not taken.
CAUTION
indicates that minor personal injury can result if proper precautions are not taken.
NOTICE
indicates that property damage can result if proper precautions are not taken.
If more than one degree of danger is present, the warning notice representing the highest degree of danger will be 
used. A notice warning of injury to persons with a safety alert symbol may also include a warning relating to property 
damage.
Qualified Personnel
The product/system described in this documentation may be operated only by personnel qualified for the specific 
task in accordance with the relevant documentation, in particular its warning notices and safety instructions. 
Qualified personnel are those who, based on their training and experience, are capable of identifying risks and 
avoiding potential hazards when working with these products/systems.
Proper use of Siemens products
Note the following:
WARNING
Siemens products may only be used for the applications described in the catalog and in the relevant technical 
documentation. If products and components from other manufacturers are used, these must be recommended or 
approved by Siemens. Proper transport, storage, installation, assembly, commissioning, operation and maintenance 
are required to ensure that the products operate safely and without any problems. The permissible ambient 
conditions must be complied with. The information in the relevant documentation must be observed.
Trademarks
All names identified by ® are registered trademarks of Siemens AG. The remaining trademarks in this publication may 
be trademarks whose use by third parties for their own purposes could violate the rights of the owner.
Disclaimer of Liability
We have reviewed the contents of this publication to ensure consistency with the hardware and software described. 
Since variance cannot be precluded entirely, we cannot guarantee full consistency.  However, the information in this 
publication is reviewed regularly and any necessary corrections are included in subsequent editions.

Security information
1
Siemens provides products and solutions with industrial security functions that support the 
secure operation of plants, systems, machines and networks.
In order to protect plants, systems, machines and networks against cyber threats, it is necessary 
to implement – and continuously maintain – a holistic, state-of-the-art industrial security 
concept. Siemens’ products and solutions constitute one element of such a concept.
Customers are responsible for preventing unauthorized access to their plants, systems, 
machines and networks. Such systems, machines and components should only be connected to 
an enterprise network or the internet if and to the extent such a connection is necessary and only 
when appropriate security measures (e.g. firewalls and/or network segmentation) are in place.
For additional information on industrial security measures that may be implemented, please 
visit 
https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurity. 
Siemens’ products and solutions undergo continuous development to make them more secure. 
Siemens strongly recommends that product updates are applied as soon as they are available 
and that the latest product versions are used. Use of product versions that are no longer 
supported, and failure to apply the latest updates may increase customer’s exposure to cyber 
threats.
To stay informed about product updates, subscribe to the Siemens Industrial Security RSS Feed 
under 
https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurity.

Introduction
2
The PowerControl library contains technological objects for controlling and visualizing 
switchgear devices in the PCS 7 environment. The block library is based on the standard 
functions of the PCS 7 Advanced Process Library V9.1 (APL). 
This manual is to be used together with the PCS 7 Advanced Process Library V9.1 Function 
Manual [1] as the APL standard functions are not described in this document.
2.1
Hardware environment
The blocks of the PowerControl library can be used in different hardware environments. 
Separate device driver libraries are available for these environments that are not contained in the 
PowerControl library (PCL).
The PowerControl library can be used in the following environments:

3.2
General block functions
3.2.1
Configuration of the faceplate and the units
The representation of the technology object faceplates (e.g. switch representation for 
PC_FEEDER) is configured directly at the function block in the CFC editor. You do this with the 
input structures FP_Visu and FP_Units.
The following settings can be configured in these two structures:
•
Switch representation with PC_FEEDER/PC_FEEDER_2B
•
Display of the interlocks in the faceplate with PC_FEEDER/PC_FEEDER_2B
•
Texts of the switch positions with PC_FEEDER/PC_FEEDER_2B
•
User views
•
Units
A detailed description of the functionalities is available in the section of the respective 
technological object.

Time stamp:
The alarms and messages of a switchgear device are output by the technological block of the PCL

If the devices are connected through PROFIBUS, the transfer of the time stamps depend on the 
PROFIBUS assignment used.

The PC_FEEDER object is used for all feed-ins or branches of a busbar. It can also be configured 
as a circuit breaker, grounding switch or disconnector. In addition, it is used for switchable 
machine contactors.
PC_FEEDER consists of the following objects:

6.1
PLC block PC_FEEDER
6.1.1
Description of PLC block PC_FEEDER
The PC_FEEDER (FB 2500) function block represents the feeder object in the PLC. The block is the 
interface between the device driver block and the remaining PCS 7 environment.
The block offers the following functions:
•
Detecting data from the device driver block
•
Providing data for the block symbol and the faceplate
•
Controlling switches of the switchgear device
•
APL modes Out of service, Local, Manual, Automatic
•
Interlocking functions
•
Handling of operator authorizations
•
Configuration of the faceplate
•
Various APL standard functions
PowerControl Library AS Manual
Function Manual, 08/2021, A5E51115858-AA

6.1.2
Interfaces
The PLC block PC_FEEDER offers the following interfaces:
1. Device driver blocks
The device driver block is connected to the PC_FEEDER block through the input "Rcv_Data" 
and the output "Snd_Data".
2. Block symbol 
The block symbol receives data from the block through the S7 connection between the PLC 
and WinCC.
3. Faceplate
The faceplate receives data from the block through the S7 connection between the PLC and 
WinCC.
4. APL interlock blocks 
The interlock blocks can be connected through the inputs "Permit", "IntLock" and "Protect".
5. Logic of the S7 program (for controlling modes, switches, etc.)
The PC_FEEDER block can receive commands from the CFC logic and makes data available to 
other blocks.
6.1.3
Configuration
Use the CFC editor to install the block in a cyclic interrupt OB (OB30 to OB38). The block is also 
installed automatically in the startup OB (OB 100).

6.1.7
Behavior of external tripping signals
External trippings from the CFC logic can be connected with the "Trip" input. The "Trip" input 
functions like the "Protect" interlock and opens Q0, if it was closed beforehand.
Similarly to the interlocks, the trigger signal is low-active:
Trip.Value = 1 → Not interlocked
Trip.Value = 0 → Interlocked, "Open Q0" command is sent
After a trigger condition the block has to be reset (see chapter Resetting the block with an 
interlock or external trigger (Page 47)).
6.1.8
Resetting the block with an interlock or external trigger
This block offers the APL standard function "Resetting the block in case of interlocks or errors". 
After a "Protect" interlock or an external trip the block has to be reset so that a close command 
can be sent to the circuit breaker Q0. 
In automatic mode resetting is carried out through a rising edge at the input "RstLi".
In manual mode resetting is only required if the function bit 31 (ResetinManual) is set and 
resetting is carried out by using the "Reset" command button in the standard view of the 
faceplate.
6.1.9
Tracking mode
Tracking mode is used to set the physically correct switch positions directly at the faceplate while 
the connection to the IED is lost. This means the current switch position can be reproduced even 
while the connection is lost.

Dynamizing the active power direction
Dynamizing the active power direction
The active power display of the corresponding PC_FEEDER block icons can be dynamically 
displayed as a function of the active power P.
The latest value for the active power P is used to display the active power direction. Depending 
on the sign of the active power, the direction display is shown in one or the other direction or is 
completely hidden if the active power = 0W.
The dynamization of the active power can be enabled or disabled using Feature.Bit20.
•
0 = Dynamization of active power direction disabled
•
1 = Dynamization of active power direction enabled
Feature.Bit21 can be used to configure the direction of the active power in the event of a 
negative value
•
0 = For a negative active power value, the arrow points downwards.
•
1 = For a negative active power value, the arrow points upwards.

6.3.1.2
Configuration of the switches
The following switches can be configured in PC_FEEDER:
•
Q0 (e.g., circuit breakers)
•
Q1 (e.g., disconnectors)
•
Q2 (e.g., additional disconnectors)
•
Q8 (e.g., grounding switches)
•
Q9 (e.g., additional grounding switches)
Switches can only be represented in fields 1-6. Up to two switches can be configured per field (for 
example, in the circuit-breaker–disconnector combination in Field 3 in the example above).
The assignment of the switches to the fields is configured with the structure elements "QX_Field" 
and "QX_SubField" of the "FP_Visu" structure that are available for each of the 5 switches.
The "QX_Field" attribute describes the number of the field in which the switch is located (possible 
values: 1-6). "QX_SubField" represents one of the two "subfields" of the "QX_Field". This attribute 
is required to represent two switches in one field.
"QX_SubField" may ONLY have the values 1 or 2. If, for example, as shown in the figure above, 
the circuit breaker (Q0) and the disconnector (Q1) are represented in field 3, the following 
configuration is required:
•
Q0_Field = 3
•
Q0_SubField = 1
•
Q1_Field = 3
•
Q1_SubField = 2
This means both switches are shown in field 3. Q0 is assigned to SubField 1 (Switch 1), Q1 is 
assigned to SubField 2 (Switch 2).

6.3.2.2
Tracking mode
Tracking mode
If the connection to the IED is lost, you can activate tracking mode to set the physically correct 
switch positions directly at the faceplate. This means the current switch position can be 
reproduced even while the connection is lost.
PC_FEEDER
6.3 PC_FEEDER faceplate
PowerControl Library AS Manual
96
Function Manual, 08/2021, A5E51115858-AA

Activate tracking mode
While a connection is lost, the standard view of the faceplate shows the button for activating 
tracking mode for the entire time the connection is lost. Once the connection is restored, the 
button is hidden once again and tracking mode is automatically deactivated.
If the button is pressed, tracking mode can be activated with the buttons at the bottom of the 
faceplate. After activation of the operating state, the buttons for setting the switch states are 
released again. The button for activating tracking mode is locked and turns purple. 
Deactivation of tracking mode is not possible while a connection is lost.
WARNING
During the entire duration of tracking mode, the corresponding interlocks (Permit, 
Interlock, Protect, Q[x]_EnaCls, Q[x]_EnaOpn, ILCK_Q[x]_Cls, ILCK_Q[x]_Opn) of the 
individual switches are deactivated. This means all operable switches can be switched by 
means of the faceplate in tracking mode, regardless of the interlock settings.
Also observe the warning notices in the section "Using tracking mode".

PC_FEEDER_2CB
7
The PC_FEEDER_2CB object is an extension of the PC_FEEDER object and is used for all infeeds 
or branches on a redundant busbar. The differences as compared to the PC_FEEDER object are:
•
The PC_FEEDER_2CB block has 2 dedicated circuit breakers (Q01 and Q02)
•
Each of the two circuit breakers has its own, separately acting APL interlocks (Permit, Protect, 
Interlock)
•
The APL interlocks of the two circuit breakers are shown separately in the standard view. 
The blocks of the PC_FEEDER can be used as driver blocks/DataCollector blocks; the interfaces 
are identical. The switch Q9 is used as the 2nd circuit breaker in the interface structures. 
PC_FEEDER_2CB consists of the following objects:
•
PLC block PC_FEEDER_2CB
•
WinCC block icons 
•
WinCC faceplate PC_FEEDER_2CB with different views
This chapter only describes the properties of the PC_FEEDER_2CB object which are different to 
those of the PC_FEEDER object.
7.1
PLC block PC_FEEDER_2CB
7.1.1
Description of PLC block PC_FEEDER_2CB
The PC_FEEDER_2CB (FB 2501) function block represents the infeed object on a redundant 
busbar in the PLC. The block is the interface between the device driver block and the remaining 
PCS 7 environment. 
The block provides the functionality of the PC_FEEDER block with the following extensions:
•
2nd dedicated circuit breaker Q02
•
Extended interlock functions for the 2nd circuit breaker Q02
•
Additional external trip signal for 2nd circuit breaker Q02
PowerControl Library AS Manual
Function Manual, 08/2021, A5E51115858-AA
105

7.1.2
Interlocks
In addition to the interlocks of the FC_FEEDER block, the PC_FEEDER_2CB block also offers the 
3 standard APL interlock functions Permit, Interlock and Protect for the 2nd circuit breaker Q02. 
All parameters of the APL interlocks are equipped with corresponding prefixes for the two circuit 
breakers Q01 and Q02 (e.g. Q01_Intl_En for the first circuit breaker, Q02_Intl_En for the 2nd 
circuit breaker). 
The interlock logic systems of Q01 and Q02 function completely independently of one another.
7.1.3
Behavior of external tripping signals
External trippings from the CFC logic system can be connected with the "Q01_Trip" or "Q02_Trip" 
input. The "Q01_Trip/Q02_Trip" inputs function like the "Protect" interlock and open Q01/Q02, 
if they were closed beforehand.
The logic systems of Q01 and Q02 function completely independently of one another.

7.2.2
Dynamizing the active power direction
Dynamizing the active power direction
The active power display of the corresponding PC_FEEDER_2CB block icons can be dynamically 
displayed as a function of the active power P.
The latest value for the active power P is used to display the active power direction. Depending 
on the sign of the active power, the direction display is shown in one or the other direction or is 
completely hidden if the active power = 0W.
The dynamization of the active power can be enabled or disabled using Feature.Bit20.
•
0 = Dynamization of active power direction disabled
•
1 = Dynamization of active power direction enabled
Feature.Bit21 can be used to configure the direction of the active power in the event of a 
negative value
•
0 = For a negative active power value, the arrow points downwards.
•
1 = For a negative active power value, the arrow points upwards.

PC_TRAFO

The PC_TRAFO object is used for all transformer protection devices. The faceplate serves only for 
visualization. No commands are implemented in the default faceplates. However, four free 
commands are available in the user-defined faceplate and in the PLC faceplate.
PC_TRAFO consists of the following objects:
•
PLC block PC_TRAFO
•
WinCC block symbols 
•
WinCC faceplate PC_TRAFO with different views
•
Device driver blocks (not part of the PCL)
8.1
PLC block PC_TRAFO
8.1.1
Description of PLC block PC_TRAFO
The PC_TRAFO (FB 2502) function block represents the transformer object in the PLC. The block 
is the interface between the device driver block and the remaining PCS 7 environment.
The block offers the following functions:
•
Detecting data from the device driver block
•
Providing data for the block symbol and the faceplate
•
Controlling switches of the switchgear device (only free commands)
•
APL operating modes Manual, Automatic
•
Interlocking functions
•
Handling of operator authorizations
•
Various APL standard functions
8.1.2
Interfaces
The PLC block PC_TRAFO offers the following interfaces:
1. Device driver blocks
The device driver block is connected to the PC_TRAFO block through the input "Rcv_Data" and 
the output "Snd_Data".
2. Block symbol 
The block symbol receives data from the block through the S7 connection between the PLC 
and WinCC.
PowerControl Library AS Manual
Function Manual, 08/2021, A5E51115858-AA
137

3. Faceplate
The faceplate receives data from the block through the S7 connection between the PLC and 
WinCC.
4. APL interlock blocks 
The interlock blocks can be connected through the "IntLock" input. 
5. Logic of the S7 program (for controlling modes, switches, etc.)
The PC_TRAFO block can receive commands from the CFC logic and makes data available to 
other blocks.
8.1.3
Configuration
Use the CFC editor to install the block in a cyclic interrupt OB (OB30 to OB38). The block is also 
installed automatically in the startup OB (OB 100).
8.1.4

8.2.2
Dynamizing the active power direction
Dynamizing the active power direction
The active power display of the corresponding PC_TRAFO block icons can be dynamically 
displayed as a function of the active power P.
The latest value for the active power P is used to display the active power direction. Depending 
on the sign of the active power, the direction display is shown in one or the other direction or is 
completely hidden if the active power = 0W.
The dynamization of the active power can be enabled or disabled using Feature.Bit20.
•
0 = Dynamization of active power direction disabled
•
1 = Dynamization of active power direction enabled
Feature.Bit21 can be used to configure the direction of the active power in the event of a 
negative value
•
0 = For a negative active power value, the arrow points downwards.
•
1 = For a negative active power value, the arrow points upwards.

PC_SYNC
9
The PC_SYNC object is used for synchronization devices. The faceplate serves only for 
visualization. No commands are implemented in the default faceplates. However, eight free 
commands are available in the user-defined faceplate and in the PLC faceplate.
PC_SYNC consists of the following objects:
•
PLC block PC_SYNC
•
WinCC block symbols 
•
WinCC faceplate PC_SYNC with different views
•
Device driver blocks (not part of the PCL)
9.1
PLC block PC_SYNC
9.1.1
Defining synchronization points
To adapt the display of synchronization points in the faceplate, the used synchronization points 
can be defined with the input "SyncGroups". The input has the type Byte. Each individual bit 
activates a synchronization point. For example, 0xFF means that all 8 synchronization points are 
displayed. With the value 0x03, only point 1 and point 2 are displayed.
9.1.2
Description of PLC block PC_SYNC
The PC_SYNC (FB 2503) function block represents the synchronization object in the PLC. The 
block is the interface between the device driver block and the remaining PCS 7 environment.
The block offers the following functions:
•
Detecting data from the device driver block
•
Providing data for the block symbol and the faceplate
•
Controlling switches of the switchgear device (only free commands)
•
APL operating modes Manual, Automatic
•
Interlocking functions
•
Handling of operator authorizations
•
Various APL standard functions
PowerControl Library AS Manual
Function Manual, 08/2021, A5E51115858-AA
169

9.1.3
Interfaces
The PLC block PC_SYNC offers the following interfaces:
1. Device driver blocks
The device driver block is connected to the PC_SYNC block through the input "Rcv_Data" and 
the output "Snd_Data".
2. Block symbol 
The block symbol receives data from the block through the S7 connection between the PLC 
and WinCC.
3. Faceplate
The faceplate receives data from the block through the S7 connection between the PLC and 
WinCC.
4. APL interlock blocks 
The interlock blocks can be connected through the "IntLock" input. 
5. Logic of the S7 program (for controlling modes, switches, etc.)
The PC_SYNC block can receive commands from the CFC logic and makes data available to 
other blocks.
9.1.4
Configuration
Use the CFC editor to install the block in a cyclic interrupt OB (OB30 to OB38). The block is also 
installed automatically in the startup OB (OB 100).
9.1.5

PC_LINE
10
The PC_LINE object is used for all differential and distance protection devices. The faceplate 
serves only for visualization. No commands are implemented in the default faceplates. However, 
four free commands are available in the user-defined faceplate and in the PLC faceplate.
PC_LINE consists of the following objects:
•
PLC block PC_LINE
•
WinCC block symbols 
•
WinCC faceplate PC_LINE with different views
•
Device driver blocks (not part of the PCL)
10.1
PLC block PC_LINE
10.1.1
Description of PLC block PC_LINE
The PC_LINE (FB 2504) function block represents the line object in the PLC. The block is the 
interface between the device driver block and the remaining PCS 7 environment.
The block offers the following functions:
•
Detecting data from the device driver block
•
Providing data for the block symbol and the faceplate
•
Controlling switches of the switchgear device (only free commands)
•
APL operating modes Manual, Automatic
•
Interlocking functions
•
Handling of operator authorizations
•
Various APL standard functions
10.1.2
Interfaces
The PLC block PC_LINE offers the following interfaces:
1. Device driver blocks
The device driver block is connected to the PC_LINE block through the input "Rcv_Data" and 
the output "Snd_Data".
2. Block symbol 
The block symbol receives data from the block through the S7 connection between the PLC 
and WinCC.
PowerControl Library AS Manual
Function Manual, 08/2021, A5E51115858-AA
207

3. Faceplate
The faceplate receives data from the block through the S7 connection between the PLC and 
WinCC.
4. APL interlock blocks 
The interlock blocks can be connected through the "IntLock" input. 
5. Logic of the S7 program (for controlling modes, switches, etc.)
The PC_LINE block can receive commands from the CFC logic and makes data available to 
other blocks.
10.1.3
Configuration
Use the CFC editor to install the block in a cyclic interrupt OB (OB30 to OB38). The block is also 
installed automatically in the startup OB (OB 100).
10.1.4
Operating modes
The PC_LINE block supports the APL standard operating modes. 
The operating mode can only be changed through the interconnections on the PLC block.

PC_BUSBAR
11
The PC_BUSBAR object represents a busbar. PC_BUSBAR does not represent a device of the 
switchgear; it only detects data from other CFC blocks. In addition a faceplate does not exist for 
this block.
PC_BUSBAR consists of the following objects:
•
PLC block PC_BUSBAR
•
WinCC block symbols 
11.1
PLC block PC_BUSBAR
11.1.1
Description of PLC block PC_BUSBAR
The PC_BUSBAR (FB 2504) function block represents the busbar object in the PLC.
The block offers the following functions:
•
Provision of data for the block symbol 
•
Various APL standard functions
11.1.2
Interfaces
The PLC block PC_BUSBAR offers the following interfaces:
1. Block symbol 
The block symbol receives data from the block through the S7 connection between the PLC 
and WinCC.
2. Logic of the S7 program (for controlling modes, switches, etc.)
The PC_BUSBAR block can receive commands from the CFC logic and makes data available to 
other blocks.
11.1.3
Configuration
Use the CFC editor to install the block in a cyclic interrupt OB (OB30 to OB38). The block is also 
installed automatically in the startup OB (OB 100).
PowerControl Library AS Manual
Function Manual, 08/2021, A5E51115858-AA
233

11.1.4
Group error
This block provides the standard APL function "Outputting group errors".
The following parameters are taken into consideration when forming the group error:
•
CSF
The group error output is GrpErr.Value.
11.1.5
Groups of input values
Up to three value groups can be connected with the PC_BUSBAR block - usually depending on the 
connected input feed. Each group consists of the following values:
•
Current (I)
•
Voltage (U)
•
Power (P)
•
Reactive power (Q)
•
Apparent power (S)
•
Frequency (F)
•
Power factor (PF)
The input groups can be activated with the "U_X_ON" inputs. Only one input group may be active 
at any given time. If several groups are activated, a message is triggered.
The output values of the block and the values displayed on the symbol follow the active group.
11.1.6
Labeling of the busbar
Labeling of the busbar is made with the structure attribute "Busbar_Desc" of the "Visu" input 
structure.

Color display of the busbar
You configure the color of the busbar with the structure "Visu" at the PC_BUSBAR function block. 
It is also possible to display the color differently depending on the status of the grounding switch 
and the voltage present. This feature uses the same hexadecimal color coding as in the WinCC 
Graphics Editor. The following structure attributes are available:

The coloring is made according to the following logic:

•
When voltage is present (U<>0), the color VoltageColor is used.
•
When no voltage is present and Earthed = 0, the ZeroVoltageColor is used.

The current color of the busbar can also be linked to other connected PCL blocks (PC_FEEDER, 
PC_FEEDER_2CB, PC_TRAFO). To do so, the output "BB_Color" at the color block PC_BUSBAR is 
linked to the input "BB_Color" at the other technological blocks.

PC_MEAS
12
The PC_MEAS block is a generic block used to represent measuring points in an electrical system. 
It does not require special driver blocks; all data existing in the automation system can be 
connected and displayed. Examples are analog input drivers, fixed wired signals, other 
communication blocks, etc.
The following measured values can be displayed:
•
Voltages phase-N-conductor
•
Voltages phase-phase
•
Currents
•
Apparent power
•
Active power
•
Reactive power
•
Total power
•
Power factor (cos phi)
•
Total cos phi
•
Frequency
•
THD-R voltage
•
THD-R current
The PC-MEAS object consists of the following components:
•
PLC block PC_MEAS
•
WinCC block symbols
•
WinCC faceplate PC-MEAS with several views
12.1
PLC block PC_MEAS
12.1.1
Description of PLC block PC_MEAS
The PC_MEAS (FB 2506) PLC block represents the PC_MEAS object in the PLC.
The block has the following functionalities:
•
Collecting data
•
Providing the data for the block symbols and the faceplate
PowerControl Library AS Manual
Function Manual, 08/2021, A5E51115858-AA
245

•
Standard APL functionalities
•
Measured value monitoring and signaling
12.1.2
Interfaces
The PLC block PC_MEAS offers the following interfaces:
1. Block symbol
The block symbol receives data from the block through the S7 connection between the PLC 
and WinCC.
2. Faceplate
The faceplate receives data from the block through the S7 connection between the PLC and 
WinCC.
3. Inputs for measured values
12.1.3
Configuration
Use the CFC editor to install the block in a cyclic interrupt OB (OB30 to OB38). The block is also 
installed automatically in the startup OB (OB 100).
12.1.4
Group error
This block provides the standard APL function "Outputting group errors".
The following parameters are taken into consideration when forming the group error:
•
CSF
•
trip
The group error output is GrpErr.Value.
12.1.5
Measured value monitoring
The PC_MEAS block provides the functionality of measured value monitoring. The user has the 
possibility of defining limits for the analog values through the faceplate or the block inputs. If the 
limits are violated in either direction, a warning or an alarm is triggered through the Alarm_8P 
functionality.

DataCollector blocks

13.1
Introduction
The DataCollector blocks are an extension of the PowerControl Library (PCL). They represent 
simulation and communication blocks and can be used for the following applications:
•
Connection of I/O modules or other signal sources to the PCL. These can be used, for example, 
to read out hard-wired protection devices or protection devices with other interfaces.
•
Simulation of values, messages and feedbacks for the technological blocks
•
Preparation and final test before commissioning without needing the real hardware.
The following blocks are available:
Block name
Description
FB No.
DC_FEEDER

FB 2562
DC_SYNC
Connection of signals for the PC_SYNC blocks
FB 2563
DC_LINE
Connection of signals for the PC_LINE blocks
FB 2564
13.2
Functionalities
The DataCollector blocks have the following functionalities:
•
Collecting and transferring data to the technological blocks
•
Generation of time stamps for the messages
•
Simulation of the switch feedbacks in simulation mode
13.3
Configuration
Use the CFC editor to install the block in a cyclic interrupt OB (OB30 to OB38). 
The DataCollector blocks are connected with the technological blocks through the "Snd_Data" 
and "Rcv_Data" structure connections.
PowerControl Library AS Manual
Function Manual, 08/2021, A5E51115858-AA

block (PC_FEEDER):

13.4
Simulation mode
The simulation mode is used to simulate feedbacks from electrical switches. This allows, for 
example, an application to be tested without connecting real switches.
The simulation mode is activated by the SimOn input.
When a command is sent by the technological block in simulation mode, the DataCollector block 
sends the corresponding feedback to the technological block.
If, for example, a switch is opened, the DataCollector block immediately gives the feedback 
"open".

13.5
Hiding non-existing values in the faceplate
Based on the signal status of the values at the block I/Os, it is possible to hide individual display 
elements in a faceplate. If the signal status is assigned the value 16#FF, then the associated 
display element is not shown in the faceplate.
Figure 13-2
Hide DataCollector display
13.6
Generation of message time stamps
The DataCollector blocks offer the following options for using time stamps with alarm and switch 
position messages:
•
System time of the automation system as basis for the time stamp
•
Use of user-defined time stamps
13.6.1
Use of the system time
The DataCollector blocks automatically generate time stamps for the incoming messages. The 
system time is used as basis in the automation system.
To use the system time as time stamp for the messages to be generated, set the following values 
at the corresponding inputs:
•
ExtTSMsg = 0 - Use internal system time for alarm messages
•
ExtTSPos = 0 - Use internal system time for switch positions

13.6.2
Use of user-defined time stamps
The DataCollector blocks give you the option of specifying your own time stamps for alarm and 
switch position messages.
To use these user-defined time stamps at the messages to be generated, set the following values 
at the corresponding inputs:
•
ExtTSMsg = 1 - Use user-defined time stamps for alarm messages
•
ExtTSPos = 1 - Use user-defined time stamps for switch positions
The time stamps for the corresponding messages can be specified at the associated TS_ (for 
example, TS_Pos0) inputs.
